text:
Alex P: Heads up — I'm experimenting with a new autoscaler/helm layout for GPU nodepools in us-west-2. thinking of switching default to spot-backed pools with on-demand fallback. anyone seen weird eviction bursts with mixed instance types? :thinking:
Mira S: We had some churn last month when the spot pool lost a large chunk. apps recovered but latency spiked. we used podDisruptionBudgets to help but not perfect.
Sam T: Do you mean changing helm values for cluster-autoscaler or doing it from the terraform module?
Alex P: Both. plan is terraform to create separate nodepools per SKU + taints, then helm cluster-autoscaler with expander: "least-waste" and scale-down conservative settings. Helm values snippet I'm trying:```yaml
autoscaler:
  enabled: true
  extraArgs:
    balance-similar-node-groups: "true"
    skip-nodes-with-local-storage: "false"
    expander: least-waste
  scaleDown:
    enabled: true
    unneededTime: 10m
    utilizationThreshold: 0.5
nodeGroups:
  - name: gpu-spot-n1
    labels:
      gpu: "true"
    taints:
      - key: "gpu"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Kai L: One caution: cluster-autoscaler + mixed spot/on-demand often needs per-node-group priorities or separate ASGs so the CA doesn't pick weird replacements. terraform resource ordering matters.
Mira S: If you make spot pools a lower priority and set max-price or use capacity-optimized allocation it helps. also make sure nodeSelector and tolerations are precise to avoid pods landing on non-gpu nodes.
Sam T: For terraform module I'd keep a module per nodepool with variables: instance_types, spot=true/false, max_price, min/max size. then data-driven helm overrides keyed by nodepool name. e.g.,```hcl
module "gpu_spot" {
  source = "git::git@.../tf-aws-nodepool.git"
  name = "gpu-spot-n1"
  instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge","p4de.24xlarge"]
  spot = true
  min_size = 0
  max_size = 50
}
```
Alex P: Thanks. question: cluster-autoscaler configmap to prefer on-demand fallback? I found `--node-group-auto-discovery` + priority config but docs are messy.
Kai L: You can fudge it by setting `--scale-down-unneeded-time` higher for spot groups or use `--expander=least-waste` and rely on capacities, but CA itself doesn't have a first-class "fallback-order". Better to expose priorities via separate nodegroup naming and custom cloudprovider configs.
Mira S: Another trick: set lower ASG max for spot and allow on-demand ASG to scale up faster (lower cooldown). We did that for batch jobs and it reduced OOM evictions.
Sam T: Don't forget kubelet config: set --eviction-hard/soft thresholds so pods on preempted nodes don't suddenly get evicted without graceful termination. Also use `podPriority` so critical services get scheduled on on-demand.
Alex P: Good call. I'm going to: 1) create tf module per pool, 2) add helm values per cluster with CA extras, 3) test in staging with forced spot reclamation. planning rollout next Tue.
deploy-bot: deploy started for staging/autoscaler-test at 2026-02-24T16:12:45Z :rocket:
Kai L: When you add the terraform changes, add a toggle in the module to optionally pin instanceTypes per AZ — that helped us avoid cross-AZ imbalance.
Mira S: Also record cost delta — spot saved ~60% but we had ~8% higher ops hours due to churn. put cost as an explicit metric in the PR template.
Alex P: Will do. I'll open a PR with terraform + helm values and tag @Kai L and @Mira S for review. action: run soak for 48h in staging, then gradual canary in prod (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
Sam T: SGTM. if you want I can add a small e2e that simulates node termination via aws ec2 terminate-instances to validate graceful rescheduling.
Alex P: Yes please, that'd be great. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
